title: Exact symmetry testing for a real matrix

model.instance: The unknown $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is an arbitrary real matrix with d at least two. Decide $A=A^T$ exactly, without a promise on distance from the symmetric matrices.

assumptions.description: An exact equality property, with no approximation promise.

model.parameter_domain_description: $d\ge2$; no tolerance parameter $\varepsilon$; success probability one for every fixed $A$.
model.description_zh: The quantity $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary, with $d\ge2$. No known distance from symmetry is required.
description_paragraphs: The matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary, with $d\ge2$. No known distance from symmetry is required.

operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: The data $d$ are public and $A$ is hidden. Exact $Av$ queries are allowed for arbitrary real vectors. No $A^{\mathsf T}u$ channel is provided.
description_paragraphs: The data $d$ are public and $A$ is hidden. Exact $Av$ queries are allowed for arbitrary real vectors. No $A^{\mathsf T}u$ channel is provided.

output.feasibility: Return the binary label symmetric exactly when $A=A^{\mathsf T}$, and nonsymmetric otherwise.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Arbitrary admissible postprocessing; the output need not have appeared as a query vector.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return $\widehat D\in\{0,1\}$ without an additional certificate.
description_paragraphs: Return $\widehat D\in\{0,1\}$, without an additional certificate.

metric.normalization: Exact binary decision, without a distance tolerance or accuracy parameter $\varepsilon$.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: The loss is $\mathbf1\{\widehat D\ne D(A)\}$ and must vanish almost surely. No approximate-symmetry promise or finite-precision threshold is imposed.
description_paragraphs: The misclassification loss is $\mathbf1\{\widehat{D}\ne D(A)\}$ and must vanish almost surely. There is no approximate-symmetry or finite-precision threshold.

proofs.title: Bilinear symmetry test using two independent continuous probes
proofs.body: Draw independent standard Gaussian vectors u,v and query Au and Av. Test whether u^T Av=v^T Au. A symmetric matrix always passes. If B=A-A^T is nonzero, the polynomial u^T Bv is not identically zero; its zero set has Lebesgue measure zero. Consequently every fixed nonsymmetric matrix is rejected with probability one. Exactly two right-multiplication queries are used.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

proofs.title: Zero-query indistinguishability of symmetric and nonsymmetric inputs
proofs.body: For d>=2, the allowed class contains both a symmetric matrix and a nonsymmetric matrix. With no queries, the output distribution is the same on these two inputs. It cannot return the two different correct labels almost surely, so at least one query is necessary.

evidence.supports: The source gives a common O(log(1/δ)) statement over finite fields and the reals. Over the reals, a nonzero quadratic polynomial vanishes on a Gaussian-null set. Consequently, two fixed queries suffice with success probability one.
